reason: three errors in the registered gate text, all found after the first run. None is a threshold retune: E1 and E2 reverse an inequality I wrote backwards relative to Theorem 1(2)-(3) of the theory chapter; E3 replaces a numerical tolerance that was below the LP solver's own feasibility tolerance and therefore unachievable by construction. Both the original and the corrected verdicts are reported.

E1_G3_direction.correct: Delta_E(n) non-DECREASING in n; hence the gate G_E(n)=1{Delta_E(n)=0} is non-increasing
E1_G3_direction.source: theory chapter Thm 1(2), eq (22b) and the paragraph at line 349
E1_G3_direction.note: Delta_E(n) is the separation available from n samples, so it grows with n. The registered wording had it backwards. The v02 run under the registered wording is reported as FAILED and is kept in results/gates_v02_asregistered.json.

E3_sion_tolerance.reason: HiGHS default primal/dual feasibility tolerance is 1e-7, so 1e-8 is not achievable on the largest LPs (K=8, n=10, 19448 count states). The per-n error is reported in results/frontier_v02.csv so the reader can see it is confined to the largest problems.

E4_permanent_obstruction_wording.registered: Delta_E(n)=Delta_E(1)=0 for all n  <=>  hulls collide at n=1
E4_permanent_obstruction_wording.correct: G_E(n)=1 for all n  <=>  there exist theta_S, theta_U with P_{theta_S} = P_{theta_U} exactly (an exact PAIRWISE single-sample collision), eq (24)
E4_permanent_obstruction_wording.note: Hull intersection at n=1 is necessary but NOT sufficient for permanent obstruction; a purely compositional intersection can dissolve at higher n. The chapter states this explicitly (line 738). The script now tests the correct statement and reports min pairwise TV.
